title: Cap. IX Arg. 7: if reprobation is antecedent and not from foresight of future impenitence, then the impenitence for which reprobates are damned flows from the reprobation decree — unjust
latin: Posita reprobatione antecedanea, et non ex praevisione futurae impoenitentiae et infidelitatis, sequetur hanc impoenitentiam et infidelitatem, propter quam reprobi damnantur, fluere ex decreto reprobationis; Est autem injustum propter illud aliquem damnare, quod ex reprobatione antecedente (quae purus putus Dei actus est) sequitur. In colloquio Hagiensi hoc urgetur a Remonstrantibus, qui videntur sentire, si ponamus reprobationem aliter factam quam ex praevisa infidelitate, consectarium esse, ut ipsam infidelitatem dictae reprobationis fructum agnoscamus. Atque hinc illa argumentatio: Si infidelitas ex reprobatione ad exitium consequitur, non potest Deus salva justitia sua reprobatos propter infidelitatem ipsorum perdere, ob id quod ex reprobatione (quae quidem est ipsius Dei opus) necessario sequitur: Reprobationem igitur ponere debemus ex praevisione infidelitatis finalis oriundam.
pass_a: Antecedent reprobation being posited, and not from foresight of future impenitence and unbelief, it will follow that this impenitence and unbelief, on account of which the reprobate are damned, flow from the decree of reprobation; But it is unjust to damn anyone on account of that which follows from antecedent reprobation (which is a pure mere act of God). In the Hague Colloquy this is urged by the Remonstrants, who seem to feel that if we place reprobation otherwise made than from foresighted unbelief, it is a corollary that we acknowledge unbelief itself as the fruit of the said reprobation. And hence that argumentation: If unbelief follows from reprobation unto destruction, God cannot with his justice safe destroy the reprobate on account of their unbelief, because of that which necessarily follows from reprobation (which indeed is the work of God himself): Therefore we ought to place reprobation as sprung from foresight of final unbelief.
pass_b: If reprobation is set as antecedent and not from foresight of future impenitence and unbelief, it will follow that the impenitence and unbelief for which the reprobate are damned flow from the reprobation decree. But it is unjust to damn anyone for what follows from antecedent reprobation — a pure mere act of God. At the Hague Colloquy the Remonstrants press this: if we place reprobation otherwise than from foresighted unbelief, the corollary is that we must own unbelief itself as fruit of that reprobation. Hence their argument: if unbelief follows from reprobation unto destruction, God cannot, his justice safe, destroy the reprobate for their unbelief, because that necessarily follows from reprobation — which is God's own work. Therefore, they say, we must place reprobation as sprung from foresight of final unbelief.

lemmas.gloss: adversaries: impenitence flows from reprobation decree
Hague Colloquy: unbelief as fruit of reprobation

title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: God foresaw reprobates would be impenitent — but that foresight is not antecedent moving cause of reprobation; unbelief sprouts from the reprobate's perverse heart
latin: Illud imprimis praemitto, Nos minime negare Deum reprobantem ab aeterno praevidisse omnes reprobatos fore impoenitentes et incredulos, sed negare hanc praevisam infidelitatem a Deo consideratam ut causam antecedaneam et motivam ipsius reprobationis. Neque tamen concedemus infidelitatem hanc pullulare ex decreto reprobantis tanquam fructum aut effectum reprobationis: sed pullulat ut malus fructus ex malo et perverso corde reprobati. Quando igitur objiciunt, Si ex reprobatione sequitur infidelitas, homines injuste damnantur propter hanc infidelitatem, ex Divino reprobationis decreto sequentem: si sequelam ordinis vel temporis intelligant, negamus consequentiam; si sequelam causalitatis, negamus infidelitatem ex reprobatione tanquam effectum ex causa consequi.
pass_a: This first of all I premise, that We by no means deny that God reprobating from eternity foresaw that all the reprobated would be impenitent and unbelieving, but deny that this foresighted unbelief was considered by God as the antecedent and moving cause of reprobation itself. Nor yet will we grant that this unbelief sprouts from the decree of the reprobating one as fruit or effect of reprobation: but it sprouts as a bad fruit from the bad and perverse heart of the reprobate. When therefore they object, If from reprobation unbelief follows, men are unjustly damned on account of this unbelief following from the Divine decree of reprobation: if they understand a sequel of order or time, we deny the consequence; if a sequel of causality, we deny that unbelief follows from reprobation as effect from cause.
pass_b: First I premise: we do not deny that God, reprobating from eternity, foresaw that all the reprobate would be impenitent and unbelieving. We deny that that foresighted unbelief was taken by God as antecedent moving cause of reprobation itself. Nor do we grant that this unbelief sprouts from the reprobating decree as fruit or effect of reprobation: it sprouts as bad fruit from the reprobate's bad perverse heart. When they object — If unbelief follows from reprobation, men are unjustly damned for that unbelief following from the divine reprobation decree — if they mean sequel of order or time, we deny the consequence; if sequel of causality, we deny that unbelief follows from reprobation as effect from cause.

lemmas.gloss: foresight of unbelief ≠ moving cause of reprobation
unbelief sprouts from reprobate's heart, not decree

title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: God elects some to be faithful and makes them so — he did not reprobate men that they might be unbelievers; Lombard Sent. 1 dist. 40–41
latin: Nam quamvis Deus eligat quosdam ut fideles essent, et per gratiam electionis eos fideles efficiat, tamen non dicendus est reprobasse homines ut infideles essent, aut reprobando eosdem infideles reddidisse. Communis enim sententia est Theologorum, quam Magister Sententiarum posuit lib. 1. dist. 40. lit. D. hisce verbis, Non enim sicut praeparavit sanctos ad justitiam percipiendam, sic praeparavit iniquos ad justitiam amittendam; quia pravitatis praeparator nunquam fuit. Et adhuc planius, dist. 41. lit. E, Quaeritur utrum sicut dicitur elegisse quosdam ut boni fierent et fideles, ita etiam concedi debeat reprobasse quosdam ut mali essent et infideles, et obdurare ut peccent; quod nullatenus concedi oportet. Non enim reprobatio ita est causa mali sicut praedestinatio est causa boni; neque obduratio ita facit hominem malum quemadmodum misericordia facit bonum.
pass_a: For although God elects certain ones that they should be faithful, and by the grace of election makes them faithful, yet he is not to be said to have reprobated men that they should be unbelievers, or by reprobating to have rendered the same unbelievers. For it is the common sentence of Theologians, which the Master of the Sentences put lib. 1. dist. 40. lit. D. in these words, For not as he prepared the saints unto receiving righteousness, so did he prepare the iniquitous unto losing righteousness; because he was never a preparer of wickedness. And still more plainly, dist. 41. lit. E, It is asked whether as it is said that he elected certain ones that they should become good and faithful, so also it ought to be granted that he reprobated certain ones that they should be evil and unbelieving, and hardens that they may sin; which by no means ought to be granted. For reprobation is not so the cause of evil as predestination is the cause of good; nor does hardening so make a man evil as mercy makes him good.
pass_b: Though God elects some that they may be faithful, and by electing grace makes them faithful, he is not to be said to have reprobated men that they might be unbelievers, or by reprobating to have made them so. That is the common sentence of theologians, which the Master of the Sentences sets (lib. 1 dist. 40 lit. D): For not as he prepared the saints to receive righteousness did he prepare the wicked to lose it — he was never a preparer of wickedness. And still plainer (dist. 41 lit. E): it is asked whether, as he is said to have elected some that they might become good and faithful, we ought also grant he reprobated some that they might be evil and unbelieving, and hardens that they may sin — which must in no wise be granted. Reprobation is not cause of evil as predestination is cause of good; nor does hardening make a man evil as mercy makes him good.

lemmas.gloss: reprobation does not aim to make unbelievers

title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: why all reprobates become unbelieving — Augustine Ad Simpl.: nothing worse infused; only what would make better is not given; Prosper
latin: Sed qui fit quod omnes reprobati semper evadunt infideles et impoenitentes, si infidelitas haec et impoenitentia non sint fructus aut effecta antecedentis reprobationis? Respondeo ex Augustino, Ad Simpl. l. 1. qu. 2. Non quod a Deo reprobante irrogetur aliquid quo sit homo deterior, sed tantum quod quo sit melior non erogetur. Non est ergo consequens, ut Deus quibus poenitentiam non dederit, resipiscentiam abstulerit; et quos non levaverit, alliserit, etc. ut optime Prosper, Ad Object. Vinc. Resp. 15. Et in eandem sententiam alibi respondet, Ad cap. Gallor. resp. 14. Infidelitatem non credentium Evangelio nequaquam ex Dei praedestinatione generari; sed omnes non-praedestinatos perire infidelitate voluntaria, non coacta, Sentent. super 14.
pass_a: But how comes it that all the reprobated always turn out unbelieving and impenitent, if this unbelief and impenitence are not fruits or effects of antecedent reprobation? I answer from Augustine, Ad Simpl. l. 1. qu. 2. Not that by God reprobating anything is inflicted whereby a man is worse, but only that that whereby he would be better is not bestowed. It is not therefore a consequence that God, from whom he has not given penitence, has taken away repentance; and those whom he has not lifted up, he has dashed down, etc. as Prosper excellently, Ad Object. Vinc. Resp. 15. And unto the same sentence elsewhere he answers, Ad cap. Gallor. resp. 14. That the unbelief of those not believing the Gospel is by no means generated from the predestination of God; but that all the non-predestined perish by voluntary, not forced, unbelief, Sentent. super 14.
pass_b: But how is it that all the reprobate always turn out unbelieving and impenitent, if that unbelief and impenitence are not fruits or effects of antecedent reprobation? I answer with Augustine (Ad Simpl. 1.2): not that God by reprobating inflicts anything by which a man is made worse, but only that what would make him better is not bestowed. So it does not follow that those to whom God has not given penitence he has robbed of repentance, or that those he has not lifted he has dashed down — as Prosper well says (Ad Object. Vinc. Resp. 15). And elsewhere to the same effect (Ad cap. Gallor. resp. 14): the unbelief of those who do not believe the Gospel is in no way generated from God's predestination; all the non-predestined perish by voluntary, not forced, unbelief (Sentent. super 14).

lemmas.gloss: nothing worse infused; better-making gift withheld

title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: Adam's rebellion, impenitence, and unbelief are born in-house — no need to fetch such effects from divine reprobation
latin: Nam omnibus filiis Adae rebellio, impoenitentia, infidelitas domi nascuntur, ut minime opus sit a reprobatione Divina hujusmodi effecta arcessere: haec enim omnia, etiam inter multa gratiae Divinae remedia et auxilia, erumpunt tamen ex corde vitiato, nisi specialis misericordiae beneficio ex electionis decreto manante sanetur, et in bono statuminetur. In argumento igitur proposito caput erroris illud est, quod sumatur, Deum reprobantem eodem prorsus modo procurare media quae ducunt postea reprobatos ad mortem aeternam, quo procurat media quae ducunt electos ad vitam aeternam: atque hinc, quia perspicuum est, Deum praedestinantem propria et speciali quadam operatione efficere in praedestinatis fidem, sanctitatem, perseverantiam reliquaque omnia, quibus tanquam mediis ad vitam pervenitur; putant etiam consequens esse, ut si Deus antecedenter aliquos reprobaverit, in iisdem efficiat infidelitatem, impoenitentiam, ceteraque omnia quibus tanquam mediis postmodum in mortem ruitur. Sed longe aliter se res habet.
pass_a: For unto all the sons of Adam rebellion, impenitence, unbelief are born at home, so that there is least need to fetch such effects from Divine reprobation: for all these things, even amid many remedies and helps of Divine grace, yet break forth from a vitiated heart, unless by the benefit of special mercy flowing from the decree of election it be healed, and established in good. In the argument proposed therefore that is the head of the error, that it is assumed that God reprobating procures in the very same manner the media which afterward lead the reprobate unto eternal death, as he procures the media which lead the elect unto eternal life: and hence, because it is clear that God predestinating by a certain proper and special operation effects in the predestined faith, holiness, perseverance and all the rest by which as by means life is reached; they think it also a consequence that if God has antecedently reprobated some, in the same he effects unbelief, impenitence, and all the rest by which as by means afterward there is a rushing unto death. But the matter stands far otherwise.
pass_b: For in all Adam's children rebellion, impenitence, and unbelief are born in-house — so there is little need to fetch such effects from divine reprobation. All these, even amid many remedies and helps of divine grace, still break out from a vitiated heart unless healed and set firm in good by the benefit of special mercy flowing from the election decree. The head of error in their argument is this assumption: that God, when he reprobates, procures in the very same way the media that later lead the reprobate to eternal death as he procures the media that lead the elect to eternal life. And since it is plain that God predestinating by a proper special operation works in the predestined faith, holiness, perseverance, and all else by which as means life is reached, they think it follows that if God has antecedently reprobated some, in them he works unbelief, impenitence, and all else by which as means they later rush to death. But the matter stands far otherwise.

lemmas.gloss: error: same mode of procuring means for elect and reprobate

title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: to reprobate is to permit by denying special grace — not to pour spiritual malice; media to death are deficient evils from us, not from God
latin: Nam reprobare est Negando gratiam specialem permittere aliquos a fine beatitudinis deficere, non infundendo malitiam spiritualem in abyssum miseriae per vim eos impellere. Huc etiam accedit, quod media quibus praedestinati ducuntur ad vitam, sunt bona quaedam supernaturalia, ac proinde non aliunde quam a Fonte boni petenda: ad Deum igitur praedestinantem pertinet providere de mediis efficacibus, quorum interventu praedestinati salventur: At media quibus reprobati in mortem ruunt, sunt mala spiritualia, sunt actiones deficientes et depravatae: ergo non a summo Bono, neque a Deo efficiente, sed ab infito nostro malo, et a causa deficiente petantur. Ineptum igitur et impium est propter antecedaneum reprobationis decretum putare, id Deo incumbere, ut producat in reprobatis infidelitatem, impoenitentiam, et id genus alia, quorum interventu damnentur. Denique, et illud sciendum est, Infidelitatem, impoenitentiam, et quicquid peccati rationem subit, dici posse media quibus ipse reprobatus sibi mortem procurat: Sed respectu Reprobantis non sunt media a Deo effecta et adhibita ad damnationem reprobati, sed potius materia quam ex se parit reprobatus, Deo praevidente et circa eandem materiam justitiam suam vindicativam exercente.
pass_a: For to reprobate is, By denying special grace, to permit some to fall short of the end of beatitude, not by pouring in spiritual malice to drive them by force into the abyss of misery. Hither also it is added, that the media by which the predestined are led unto life are certain supernatural goods, and therefore to be sought from nowhere else than from the Fountain of good: unto God therefore predestinating it pertains to provide concerning efficacious media, by whose intervention the predestined may be saved: But the media by which the reprobate rush unto death are spiritual evils, are deficient and depraved actions: therefore they are to be sought not from the highest Good, nor from God as efficient, but from our implanted evil, and from a deficient cause. It is therefore inept and impious on account of the antecedent decree of reprobation to think that it incumbs upon God to produce in the reprobate unbelief, impenitence, and other things of that kind, by whose intervention they are damned. Finally, this also is to be known, that Unbelief, impenitence, and whatever falls under the account of sin, can be called media by which the reprobate himself procures death unto himself: But in respect of the Reprobating One they are not media effected and applied by God unto the damnation of the reprobate, but rather matter which the reprobate brings forth from himself, God foreseeing and about the same matter exercising his vindicative justice.
pass_b: To reprobate is, by denying special grace, to permit some to fall short of beatitude's end — not by pouring spiritual malice in to drive them by force into the abyss of misery. Add this: the media by which the predestined are led to life are supernatural goods, and so to be sought only from the Fountain of good — it belongs to God predestinating to provide efficacious media by whose intervention the predestined are saved. But the media by which the reprobate rush to death are spiritual evils — deficient, depraved acts — and so are sought not from the highest Good, nor from God as efficient, but from our implanted evil and a deficient cause. It is therefore inept and impious, because of an antecedent reprobation decree, to think God must produce in the reprobate unbelief, impenitence, and the like by which they are damned. Finally: unbelief, impenitence, and whatever counts as sin can be called media by which the reprobate himself procures his own death. But respecting the Reprobating One they are not media God effects and applies unto the reprobate's damnation — rather matter the reprobate brings forth from himself, God foreseeing and about that matter exercising his vindicative justice.

lemmas.gloss: reprobation = permit by denying special grace, not infuse malice
media to death from deficient evil in us, not from God
